1	# The loop
2	
3	A "loop engineering" setup: a written spec + a stop condition, run by a
4	script, with a **maker** and a separate **checker** so the implementer never
5	grades its own homework. (Term popularized by [Peter Steinberger](https://x.com/steipete)
6	and [Addy Osmani](https://addyosmani.com/blog/loop-engineering/), writing
7	about putting AI coding agents on repeat.)
8	
9	## Glossary
10	
11	New to this vocabulary? Skim this once before the tables below.
12	
13	| Term | Plain-English meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| **Maker** | The agent that writes the diff for one task. |
16	| **Checker** | A *different* agent that reviews that diff before it can merge — never the same one that wrote it. |
17	| **Harness** | The adapter script (`loop/harnesses/<name>.sh`) wrapping one CLI (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, …) so `run.sh` can call it generically as maker, checker, or council member. |
18	| **Ring** | The review rotation: `LOOP_KIT_HARNESSES` order decides who checks whom (each member is checked by the next, wrapping around). |
19	| **Worktree** | An isolated `git worktree` + branch created per task, so a bad run never touches your main branch directly. |
20	| **Backoff** | A recorded cooldown when a harness looks rate-limited, so the loop stops hammering it. |
21	| **Adjudication** | The policy that turns the checker's bug reports into a verdict (`approve` / `request_changes` / `block_human`) — folded into the same reviewer call, not a separate step. |
22	| **Council** | A read-only, parallel fan-out of one question to several models for independent opinions — no maker/checker relationship, just `loop/council.sh`. |
23	| **Require-human-review path** | A path pattern that always routes to a human, regardless of what maker/checker conclude. |
24	
25	Coming from the "graph engineering" conversation and looking for terms
26	like *node*, *DAG*, or *fan-out/fan-in*? The root README's "Loop, or
27	graph?" section maps those onto this list — not needed to use the kit,
28	just a translation for a specific audience.
29	
30	## Concepts
31	
32	### Harnesses
33	
34	Which CLIs (and models) sit in the rotation is **config**, not code:
35	`LOOP_KIT_HARNESSES` in `loop.config.sh` (default `codex claude cursor`).
36	
37	| Syntax | Meaning |
38	|---|---|
39	| `cursor` | Bare harness — uses that harness's project default model |
40	| `cursor:grok-4.5-high` | Pin a specific model (same for `copilot:…` / `opencode:…`) |
41	| ≥2 members | Required (not necessarily ≥2 distinct harnesses) |
42	| Identical members | Forbidden (genuine self-review) |
43	
44	One multi-model CLI can fill multiple seats:
45	
46	```sh
47	LOOP_KIT_HARNESSES="cursor:grok-4.5-high cursor:claude-4.5-sonnet"
48	LOOP_KIT_HARNESSES="copilot:gpt-5.4 copilot:claude-sonnet-4.6"
49	```
50	
51	Each harness is `loop/harnesses/<name>.sh`. Built-ins: `codex`, `claude`,
52	`cursor`, `copilot`, `opencode`. Add your own via `loop/new_harness.sh <name>` /
53	`TEMPLATE.sh.example`.
54	
55	- One atomic task per run, fresh context every time
56	- State lives on disk + git — never in the model's head
57	- Downstream of the maker (verify → require-human-review gate → review →
58	  merge) is identical for every harness; only the attempt step differs
59	
60	**Sandbox note (built-ins):** Codex runs inside an OS-level sandbox
61	(`-s workspace-write`) that restricts what it can touch outside the
62	worktree, even before a human looks at the diff. Claude / Cursor / Copilot
63	/ opencode have no such restriction — they can run any command the worktree
64	allows, same as a normal terminal session — so they lean entirely on
65	worktree isolation plus the checker step for safety. Reserve those makers
66	for well-scoped, non-sensitive work.
67	
68	### Maker complexity tiers
69	
70	Optional task frontmatter `complexity: quick|default|gnarly` picks

560	Managed skill: `LOOP_KIT_SKILLOPT_SKILL_PATH` (default
561	`.claude/skills/project-loop/SKILL.md`).
562	
563	SkillOpt only mutates the protected `<!-- SKILLOPT-SLEEP:LEARNED -->`
564	block. Standing procedures + quality bar above that block stay yours.
565	
566	### Domain-specific review guidance, without routing by path
567	
568	If a domain in your codebase (auth, billing, a migration-prone schema)
569	keeps needing sharper review than the rest, the fix this kit is built
570	for is **not** hardcoding "always route `src/auth/` to member X because
571	it's better at this" — that preference goes stale the moment models
572	change, and different projects would want different answers anyway. The
573	fix is encoding the domain knowledge itself as a durable, model-agnostic
574	instruction, so *whichever* member the ring happens to route to applies
575	it. Two levers, with different reach:
576	
577	| Lever | Reach | Evolves via |
578	|---|---|---|
579	| `review_mandate.partial.md` (numbered adversarial items) | Every harness, every review — this text is rendered directly into the prompt every reviewer receives, regardless of CLI. | Hand-edit only; SkillOpt never touches it. |
580	| `.claude/skills/project-loop/SKILL.md` (Standing procedures + `LEARNED` block) | **Claude Code only** — loaded automatically when `claude` is the acting harness (its `description` frontmatter is written to match "implementing or reviewing loop queue tasks"), or during an interactive Claude Code session in the repo. Codex/Cursor/Copilot/opencode never read it. | Standing procedures: hand-edit. `LEARNED` block: SkillOpt-Sleep, from real loop/log evidence, gated by held-out validation + your `adopt`. |
581	
582	For guidance that must apply no matter which ring member reviews the
583	diff (e.g. "diffs touching `src/auth/` must verify session tokens are
584	never logged"), add it as a numbered item to `review_mandate.partial.md`
585	— same place you'd add any other recurring failure mode, per "Not
586	prompted (edit by hand)" in the root README.
587	
588	To have SkillOpt-Sleep *discover and propose* that kind of domain-specific
589	rule instead of writing it by hand: accumulate real `done/`/`blocked/`
590	tasks that touch the domain, then run `skillopt_sleep.sh run --backend
591	claude` (or another real backend). The mined evidence already carries
592	each task's file paths (via its Scope) and outcome, so a domain that
593	keeps producing `request_changes`/`blocked` outcomes is exactly the
594	pattern the held-out gate is designed to surface as a proposal — one you
595	review and `adopt`, not a routing rule you maintain by hand.
596	
597	That said, an adopted rule still only reaches Claude Code, per the table
598	above. If it needs to reach every harness, copy it into
599	`review_mandate.partial.md` yourself once you've adopted it.
600	
601	Claude Code also gets a thin `.claude/skills/skillopt-sleep/` pointer
602	(same pattern as `council` / `new-task`).
